title: Indian Hotels Company Ltd - 500850 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IHCL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% to INR2,845 crores with EBITDA margin of 37%; FY27 guidance is double-digit (12-14%) revenue growth.
summary.overview: IHCL reported its 16th consecutive quarter of record performance, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 14% YoY to INR2,845 crores and EBITDA up 15% to INR1,052 crores. Standalone Q4 RevPAR grew 12%, the company said, with standalone EBITDA margin up 160 bps to 49.5%. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16% to INR9,971 crores and consolidated PAT crossed INR2,000 crores for the first time. Management said March and early April were weak due to the West Asia conflict, with recovery from mid-April, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 12-14%, with Q1 FY27 growth expected above 12%.

segments.name: Standalone hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,721 crores with 12% RevPAR growth and 49.5% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue INR5,640 crores (+10%) and EBITDA margin 45.1% (+120 bps).

segments.name: New businesses (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Stays & Trails, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR753 crores, up 25%, with a 31% four-year CAGR. Ginger Mumbai Airport crossed INR100 crores revenue at a 56% EBITDA margin; Qmin has 100-plus outlets and GMV near INR200 crores.

segments.name: TajSATS (catering)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of 16% was flattered by an airport levy accounting change; management said growth would have been about 11-12% on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Ginger consolidated (Roots and Ginger Mumbai Airport)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR700-709 crores with a very high EBITDA margin; management now reports Ginger on a consolidated basis rather than Roots standalone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guided at 12-14%, with management confident of delivering it.
Like-for-like RevPAR planned at high-single-digit growth (about 7-9%) on a one- to two-year view; ARR is the main lever.
Non-like-for-like growth of about 4-5% expected in FY27 from around 60 hotel openings, and acquisitions expected to add over INR250 crores incremental revenue.
Q1 FY27 revenue growth expected to be above 12%, with domestic demand stronger than international.
Capex of INR1,000-1,200 crores annually; Ginger portfolio target of 250 hotels under development or operating by end-FY27.
Next Capital Market Day to be announced within weeks; capital-light share guided at 63% on the prior framework, with ANK & Pride amendments pointing toward about 70%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex over INR1,000 crores: about INR650 crores on renovations, routine maintenance and digital, and the rest on greenfield projects.
Over the last three years, more than INR2,500 crores invested in capex; more than INR500 crores deployed across four acquisitions.
Portfolio of over 630 hotels and 64,000-plus keys; pipeline of 31,000-plus keys, 93% capital-light; 68% of operating portfolio under managed or asset-light formats.
FY27 openings of about 60 hotels (around 5,000 keys, give or take 5%); Frankfurt delayed to around June 2026; 15 ANK & Pride conversions expected to open in Q1 FY27.
Atmantan and ANK & Pride integration on track, with benefits expected in H2 FY27; President Mumbai renovation completed.
demand_pricing: Goa grew about 25% in April (some hotels 30%+); Mumbai and Delhi face high bases after strong prior years; Dubai and Maldives are down, London is okay, and domestic is strong.
West Asia conflict cost about INR40-50 crores of consolidated revenue and close to INR100 crores on an enterprise basis from last-minute event cancellations and rescheduling.

Foreign tourists are about 30% of standalone guests and this share has not moved much; management says foreign business arrivals are rising while leisure tourist arrivals remain below pre-COVID levels.
Rupee-denominated portal pricing; domestic drive vacations and MICE consolidation into domestic resorts are supporting demand.

Management says supply is tight for the foreseeable future, so RevPAR should grow at least at inflation; revenue management and a website channel shift added about 2 percentage points to distribution mix.
Lands End Mumbai runs at 90%+ occupancy, so growth there is rate-led.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and current trading, and what drives FY27 growth of 12-14%?
qa_highlights.answer: March and early April were difficult, with stability from mid-April and strong growth since. Management built the guide from key account rates, wedding bookings on the books, about 4-5% non-like-for-like growth from openings, and renovated inventory; ARR is the swing factor.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company cut the FY27 openings count?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is roughly 5,000 keys on average per year, give or take 5%. Platform partnerships could add 300-400 keys, and most openings are management contracts, so the P&L impact is small.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ANK & Pride portfolio change the long-term capital-light mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix moved toward 70% capital-light from the 63% target at the Analyst Day, because ANK & Pride is largely capital-light with only a few owned hotels. The change is additive and does not reflect any sale of capital-heavy assets.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve and is there operating leverage left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is still room for margin improvement because the newer brands are still scaling and acquisition costs were high. It is comfortable with the 35% consolidated margin provided new brands are not built with upfront capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q1 FY27 trading and the MICE cancellation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 revenue growth above 12%, with domestic outpacing international. Some MICE business was deferred rather than lost, such as the company's own hospitality conference; some nights are permanently lost.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and its effect on international travel, Dubai transit traffic and London hotels.
Aviation cost and capacity cuts by domestic carriers, which could hit travel demand and pricing.
Frankfurt opening slipping to around June 2026 and the pace of the 60-hotel opening plan.
Mumbai and Delhi high bases, which could slow like-for-like growth.
Clarity of the new Capital Market Day guidance on ROCE and the capital-light mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the medium term, with guidance tempered by explicit caution on West Asia impacts in March-April. Management was candid on the weak start to Q1 and deflected some questions on specific numbers, e.g. the segment breakdown and the 7-9% ARR bridge, saying they are an art rather than a science.
key_quotes: We remain fairly confident that we will again deliver double-digit growth between 12%, let's say, and 14% in the FY '27 fiscal.
The business was a bit sluggish. I would say March was a difficult month. Beginning of April was difficult.
This time, we have none, and we have a lot of cash. So, it might throw other opportunities.
